title: Tunisia’s largest Commonwealth war cemetery lies where the front stood still for months
body: The [Commonwealth War Graves Commission](https://admin.cwgc.org/visit-us/find-cemeteries-memorials/cemetery-details/47314/medjez-el-bab-war-cemetery/) cemetery at **Medjez-el-Bab**, about 60 km west of Tunis on the road to Le Kef, is the largest Commonwealth war cemetery in Tunisia. Why there? Medjez-el-Bab marked the limit of the Allied advance on Tunis in December 1942, and it stayed on the front line until the Allied advances of April and May 1943. The cemetery holds 2,903 Commonwealth servicemen of the Second World War, buried or commemorated; 385 of the burials are unidentified. Within it, the Medjez-el-Bab Memorial bears the names of almost 2,000 men with no known grave: soldiers of the British First Army who died in Algeria and Tunisia between 8 November 1942 and 13 May 1943, and of the Eighth Army from 20 February 1943. Eighth Army men who went missing in Tunisia before that date are named on the Alamein Memorial in Egypt. Sir Hubert Worthington designed the cemetery and the memorial. The commission is now replanting the cemetery with drought-tolerant plants, cutting its irrigated lawn by 75%.

slides.question: How many Commonwealth servicemen are buried or commemorated at Medjez-el-Bab War Cemetery, in Tunisia?
slides.explanation: 2,903 of the Second World War, by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission’s count; 385 of the burials are unidentified. Its memorial names almost 2,000 more.

slides.alt: Animation on a pale sky and Portland stone: a schematic map of northern Tunisia with the front at Medjez-el-Bab, a lawn of headstones as a grid, the memorial's panels of names, the dates of the First and Eighth Armies, the Cross of Sacrifice and the Stone of Remembrance, then a lawn replanted.

slides.prompt: Pick the army and the date a missing soldier died. Find the first day an Eighth Army man is named at Medjez-el-Bab.
slides.takeaway: 20 February 1943. Before it, Eighth Army men missing in Tunisia are named on the Alamein Memorial in Egypt; First Army men are always named at Medjez-el-Bab.

slides.heading: About 13 in 100 burials at Medjez-el-Bab are unidentified

events.text: The advance on Tunis stops at Medjez
The last date on the memorial

slides.question: An Eighth Army soldier went missing in Tunisia in January 1943. Which memorial names him?
slides.explanation: The Alamein Memorial names Eighth Army men missing in Tunisia up to 19 February 1943. From 20 February 1943 they are named at Medjez-el-Bab.
